question: Despite the fact that in Galicia only 5 % of agricultural land is used for organic production, the demand for transitions to this type of production largely exceeds the aid provided for under the CAP. In 2022, only EUR 3.18 million in aid was allocated in Galicia, compared to the necessary EUR 5.6 million to cover all applications submitted.

This resulted in a lack of aid for 43 % of the hectares applied for, something which could lead to the closure of undertakings owing to the significant investment made and incompatibility with other aid. Despite this serious situation, the Xunta de Galicia took the unilateral decision not to pay the aid pledged to the sector in 2022, deviating from the European strategy to achieve 25 % organic production by 2030.

The sector has reacted with protests and legal action. In view of this situation, what measures does the Commission intend to take to ensure that the Xunta de Galicia guarantees the payment of aid to these producers and that the objectives set for organic production are met?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.2.2024) The Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) recognises the important role of organic farming in supporting the sustainable development of rural areas and agriculture, and in contributing to more environmentally friendly farming practices.

Both the Farm to Fork1 and the Biodiversity2 Strategies include the explicit aspirational target of 25% of the EU agricultural area under organic production by 2030, taking into account different starting positions across Member States. To support the achievement of this target, the Commission adopted on 25 March 2021 the action plan for the Development of Organic Production3.

It includes 23 actions to stimulate organic production and consumption. The European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development is implemented under shared management. Specific aspects of programme implementation, such as allocation of the budget, fall under the responsibility of the Member States, in compliance with the applicable regulatory requirements.

It is the Commission’s understanding that all beneficiaries whose application was accepted were paid. The Spanish authorities have made repeated efforts to increase the support for organic production in Galicia.

In the first modification of the CAP strategic plan approved on 30 August 2023, the total budget of the organic intervention dedicated to Galicia was again increased by more than 93% compared to the first version. There are thus now considerably more funds available to support organic production in Galicia.
